fragments.text: Ted Nelson asserts that all intellectual structures and hierarchies are arbitrary accidents, contrasting with Engelbart and Pask who assumed natural hierarchies in subjects should be accentuated.
Ted Nelson defines Computer Lib as the project of making people freer through computers.
IBM's adoption of EBCDIC was primarily a strategic move to render the 360 system incompatible with other systems and terminals.
IBM holds a near-monopoly position in the computer field, selling 65 to 70 percent of all computers and programs, which allows it to define the technology for the general public.
Ted Nelson argues that the 'inverted file' is a misnomer that exposes the computer industry's pathological attachment to linear sequence.
Ted Nelson asserts that the computer is used as a General Scapegoat to cover up human decisions that are made for convenience rather than technical necessity.
